pr.title: fix(sampling): align indexed top-k and speculative metrics
pr.body:
## 📌 Description

This PR fixes two independent sampling inconsistencies.

### Keep `top_k_first` semantics stable when `indices` is provided

The large-vocabulary fast path uses radix top-k and retains exactly `k` entries. It previously rejected every call with `indices`, so adding even an identity mapping routed the same probabilities through `top_k_renorm_probs` instead. That fallback retains every entry equal to the k-th threshold.

Consequently, a boundary tie could change the sampling distribution solely because `indices` was present. For example, with `V=65536`, `k=1`, `top_p=1`, and probabilities `[3/8, 3/8, 1/4, 0, ...]`, the fast path selects one of the two maximum entries while the indexed fallback renormalizes both to `[1/2, 1/2]`.

The fix allows valid same-device int32/int64 index vectors to use the existing fast path. Top-k is still computed once for each unique source row; `indices` is passed through the compact top-p sampling step, and sampled compact indices are mapped back through the corresponding source row. Per-row `top_k`/`top_p` validation and the returned index dtype are preserved. This keeps exact-k tie behavior independent of an otherwise identity-preserving row mapping without expanding full-vocabulary or compact rows.

### Do not count the first speculative rejection twice

`chain_speculative_sampling` first samples the accepted prefix and records the first rejected position in `pos`. Its independent acceptance-metric loop then started from `pos` and sampled that already rejected token again. For one draft token with true acceptance probability `alpha=0.5`, the reported expectation became `alpha + (1-alpha)alpha = 0.75` instead of `0.5`.

The metric loop now excludes `pos` from the count. It deliberately still consumes the same random draw at that position, preserving the RNG state used by the subsequent correction sample and therefore preserving fixed-seed generated tokens.

### Compatibility and performance notes

- For indexed calls with vocabulary size ≥ 65536 and `k ≤ 256`, a fixed seed/offset now yields different tokens than before because the call takes the exact-k fast path; the sampling distribution is unchanged.
- `output_accepted_token_num` will read lower for callers comparing acceptance rates across versions because the previous value double-counted some first rejections. Generated output tokens are unchanged by this metric fix.
- On SM100 with `V=128256` and `k=50`, using 2-D advanced indexing for non-indexed calls regressed logits from 0.151 to 0.169 ms through 128 rows and from 0.160 to 0.171 ms at 256 rows; probs regressed from 0.170 to 0.187 ms. The final revision keeps the original single-`gather` mapping when `indices` is absent and uses 2-D indexing only for indexed calls, restoring non-indexed timings to within 0.006 ms of the previous fast path. Indexed calls pass `indices` through the compact sampler without expanding compact rows. Measurements are from SM100 and have not been repeated on B200.

# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"

      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
        id: cuda-versions
        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check Skip Conditions
        id: check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 0
          fi

          # Use PR event SHAs for reliable diff (avoids issues with origin refs)
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          # TODO (yongwww): Add back ^\.github/ before merging to main
          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"

          SKIP=true
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then
              SKIP=false
              break
            fi
          done <<< "$CHANGED"

          echo "skip=$SKIP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          if [ "$SKIP" == "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Skipping build - only docs/config files changed"
          fi

      # skip_aot / skip_gpu dispatch inputs have to drop entries before the
      # matrix expands - a job-level `if` cannot see the matrix context, and
      # skipping inside the job would still claim a runner first.
      - name: Build Test Matrix
        id: matrix
        env:
          SKIP_AOT: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_aot }}
          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
          # Targets requested by the triggering `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment,
          # already validated in the step above. Empty for an unparameterised run.
          REQUESTED_TEST_PATH: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
          H100_ON_PRS: 'true'
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          RUN_H100=false
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$H100_ON_PRS" != "true" ]; then
            RUN_H100=false
            echo "::notice title=H100 lane disabled on PRs::H100 tests run only in scheduled main runs and manual workflow_dispatch runs until runner capacity is restored" >&2
          fi
          echo "h100_disabled=$([ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ] && echo false || echo true)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # A targeted run on a lane never tests more than that lane's bare run: H100
          # gets the request as-is (its bare run covers tests/); A10G and T4 get it
          # intersected with their shard lists, and a lane left with nothing is skipped.
          # A10G is intersected per shard: each shard whose files overlap the request
          # runs as its own job, so a targeted run keeps the bare run's balancing and
          # -k splits, and shards left with nothing are not scheduled.
          A10G_SCOPES=(); T4_SCOPE=""; H100_SCOPE=""
          if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -n "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then
            for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
              A10G_SCOPES[$shard]=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
                --scripts "scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part${shard}.sh" \
                --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
              echo "A10G shard ${shard} targeted scope: ${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-<none: shard not scheduled>}"
            done
            T4_SCOPE=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
              --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh \
              --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
            echo "T4 targeted scope:   ${T4_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"
            # tests/cpu belongs to the CPU Unittest lane, which runs on every run.
            # The H100 lane ignores it, so drop it from the H100 scope here: a
            # request naming only tests/cpu then schedules no H100 job instead of
            # one that collects nothing.
            H100_SCOPE=$(tr ' ' '\n' <<< "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" \
              | grep -Ev '^tests/+cpu(/|$)' | paste -sd ' ' - || true)
            echo "H100 targeted scope: ${H100_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"
          fi
          {
            if [ "$SKIP_AOT" != "true" ]; then
              for arch in x64 arm64; do
                for cuda in $(jq -r '.[].label' <<< "${RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX}"); do
                  # Runtime entries land before their multi-arch image is
                  # published. The release-ci-docker workflow adds the tag in
                  # its generated follow-up PR; only then can AOT consume it.
                  if ! grep -q "^flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${cuda}:" ci/docker-tags.yml; then
                    echo "::notice title=AOT image not published::Skipping ${cuda}; ci/docker-tags.yml has no published image yet" >&2
                    continue
                  fi
                  jq -nc --arg arch "$arch" --arg cuda "$cuda" '{
                    name: "AOT Build Import (\($arch), \($cuda))",
                    kind: "aot",
                    runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", $arch, "cpu", "on-demand"],
                    cuda: $cuda,
                    script: "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh",
                    timeout: 360
                  }'
                done
              done
            fi

            # tests/cpu runs on every run, whatever scope was requested. Its
            # tests check contracts across modules (package parity, stub
            # configs, wrapper attributes), so a change in one directory breaks
            # a CPU test that a scope naming that directory would not select.
            # It needs no GPU and takes about 5 minutes on a CPU runner, and
            # through fail-fast it stops the GPU lanes early when it fails.
            # The GPU lanes leave it out: the H100 lane ignores tests/cpu and
            # the A10G/T4 shard lists name no file under it.
            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ]; then
              jq -nc '{
                name: "CPU Unittest",
                kind: "cpu",
                gpu_name: "CPU",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "cpu", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                test_path: "tests/cpu",
                timeout: 60
              }'
            fi

            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -z "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then
              for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
                jq -nc --arg shard "$shard" '{
                  name: "JIT Unittest \($shard) (A10G)",
                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "A10G",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
                  timeout: 360
                }'
              done

              jq -nc '{
                name: "JIT Unittest (T4)",
                kind: "gpu",
                gpu_name: "T4",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh",
                timeout: 360
              }'

              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ]; then
                jq -nc '{
                  name: "JIT Unittest (H100)",
                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  timeout: 480
                }'
              fi
            elif [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ]; then
              # A `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment retargets the GPU lanes at those
              # paths. There is deliberately no arch selection: tests carry their own
              # arch guards (is_sm90a_supported() and friends) and skip themselves where
              # unsupported - nobody has to keep a path-to-arch mapping in sync with the
              # tests. Per-lane scopes (A10G_SCOPES / T4_SCOPE) are computed above the
              # brace group, which is piped into jq and so runs in a subshell.
              #
              # A10G runs its bare-run shard scripts, restricted to the scope through
              # JIT_TEST_SCOPE (see scripts/infra/jit_test_logging.sh). T4 and H100 use
              # task_run_unit_tests.sh, the script that forwards "$@" into TEST_PATH.
              #
              # This step does NOT parse the PR body. Turning a declared scope into paths
              # happens once, in whoever issues the trigger (a reviewer, or the screening
              # watcher posting under its own identity). CI runs what it is told.
              for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
                if [ -n "${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-}" ]; then
                  jq -nc --arg shard "$shard" --arg test_path "${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]}" '{
                    name: "Targeted Unittest \($shard) (A10G)",
                    kind: "gpu",
                    gpu_name: "A10G",
                    runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
                    cuda: "cu129",
                    script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
                    test_path: $test_path,
                    timeout: 360
                  }'
                fi
              done
              if [ -n "${T4_SCOPE}" ]; then
                jq -nc --arg test_path "${T4_SCOPE}" '{
                  name: "Targeted Unittest (T4)",
                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "T4",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  test_path: $test_path,
                  timeout: 360
                }'
              fi
              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ] && [ -n "${H100_SCOPE}" ]; then
                jq -nc --arg test_path "${H100_SCOPE}" '{
                  name: "Targeted Unittest (H100)",
                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  test_path: $test_path,
                  timeout: 480
                }'
              fi
            fi
          } | jq -sc '{include: .}' > matrix.json

          echo "matrix=$(cat matrix.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "count=$(jq '.include | length' matrix.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          jq -r '.include[].name' matrix.json

          # Provider spec lint: one quick lane per published CUDA image, ahead of the
          # hours-long AOT builds it guards, so a spec naming a CUDA target its
          # provider cannot carry fails the PR in minutes. Dropped with the AOT lanes.
          {
            if [ "$SKIP_AOT" != "true" ]; then
              for cuda in $(jq -r '.[].label' <<< "${RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX}"); do
                if grep -q "^flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${cuda}:" ci/docker-tags.yml; then
                  jq -nc --arg cuda "$cuda" '{cuda: $cuda}'
                fi
              done
            fi
          } | jq -sc '{include: .}' > spec-lint-matrix.json
          echo "spec_lint_matrix=$(cat spec-lint-matrix.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "spec_lint_count=$(jq '.include | length' spec-lint-matrix.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Tests - AOT build imports and GPU unit tests
  #
  # Every test is one entry of a single matrix so that fail-fast cancels all of
  # them on the first failure. As separate jobs, fail-fast is scoped per group
  # and the other groups keep running on billed on-demand capacity long after
  # the result is known. Entries still start in parallel; nothing is serialized.
  # Scheduled runs on main turn fail-fast off: they exist to report every broken
  # lane, not the first one.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
    needs: [gate, setup]
    if: |
      needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.skip_build != 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.test_count != '0'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      # Scheduled runs on main request the compile-cache upload role (see
      # "Get compile cache upload credentials"). The role's trust policy, not
      # this file, restricts it to refs/heads/main: a pull request run, even
      # one that edits this workflow, gets a token whose subject the policy
      # rejects.
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.test_matrix) }}
    env:
      DOCKER_IMAGE: flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${{ matrix.cuda }}:${{ needs.setup.outputs.docker_tag }}
      MATRIX_ARCH: ${{ matrix.runner[2] }}
      MATRIX_CUDA: ${{ matrix.cuda }}
      CI_GPU_NAME: ${{ matrix.gpu_name }}
      MATRIX_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
      TEST_SCRIPT: ${{ matrix.script }}
      # Empty for every lane except the experimental one. Quoted at the use site and
      # never interpolated into script text - it originates from the PR body.
      TEST_PATH_ARG: ${{ matrix.test_path }}
      # GPU lanes route their JIT compiles through the AOT lanes' S3 sccache.
      # On unless the repository variable FLASHINFER_GPU_TEST_SCCACHE is '0',
      # which turns it off for A/B timing without a code change. The `|| '1'`
      # matters: an unset variable is null, and `null != '0'` is false because
      # mismatched types are compared as numbers (null and '0' both become 0).
      # The CPU lane compiles nothing, so it skips sccache too.
      GPU_TEST_SCCACHE: ${{ matrix.kind != 'aot' && matrix.kind != 'cpu' && (vars.FLASHINFER_GPU_TEST_SCCACHE || '1') != '0' && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - name: Cleanup
        if: matrix.kind != 'h100'
        run: |
          # Stop all Docker containers to free memory
          docker stop $(docker ps -q) 2>/dev/null || true
          docker rm $(docker ps -aq) 2>/dev/null || true
          # Clean workspace and caches
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/* || true
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/.[!.]* || true
          rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer_jit || true
          docker image prune -f || true
          docker builder prune -f --filter "until=24h" || true
          nvidia-smi || true

      - name: Cleanup
        if: matrix.kind == 'h100'
        run: |
          # Shared multi-runner node: only stop containers started by THIS runner (identified by workspace mount)
          for cid in $(docker ps -q); do
            if docker inspect "$cid" --format '{{json .Mounts}}' 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "${{ github.workspace }}/"; then
              docker stop "$cid" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          done
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/* || true
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/.[!.]* || true
          rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer_jit || true
          docker container prune -f 2>/dev/null || true
          docker image prune -f || true
          docker builder prune -f --filter "until=24h" || true
          echo "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
          nvidia-smi -i "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES" || true

      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.checkout_sha }}
          # Self-hosted runners keep the workspace between jobs, so the token
          # must not be left behind in .git/config. Nothing here uses git after
          # checkout. Submodules initialize after source snapshot verification.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Prepare selected source and submodules
        env:
          SELECTED_BASE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_base }}
          SELECTED_TREE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SELECTED_BASE" ]; then
            [[ "$SELECTED_BASE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "$SELECTED_TREE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
            PINNED_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = true ]; then
              git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin "$PINNED_HEAD" "$SELECTED_BASE"
            fi
            git cat-file -e "${SELECTED_BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$SELECTED_BASE"
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$PINNED_HEAD"
            [ "$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')" = "$SELECTED_TREE" ]
          fi
          git submodule update --init --recursive

      - name: Show Node Info
        run: ./scripts/infra/task_show_node_info.sh
        env:
          NODE_NAME: ${{ runner.name }}
          WORKSPACE: ${{ github.workspace }}
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}

      - name: Run Test
        if: matrix.kind == 'aot'
        env:
          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET }}
          SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION }}
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          # Provider builds overlapped per job (see the script). The repository
          # variable AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY overrides it, and 1 restores the
          # serial loop, for A/B timing without a code change.
          AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY: ${{ vars.AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY || '2' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" != "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh" ]; then
            echo "::error::Unexpected AOT test script: ${TEST_SCRIPT}"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
          bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" \
            -e SCCACHE_BUCKET "${SCCACHE_BUCKET}" \
            -e SCCACHE_REGION "${SCCACHE_REGION}" \
            -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
            -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
            -e SCCACHE_STATS_DIR /workspace/sccache-stats \
            -e AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY "${AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY}" \
            --no-gpu "./scripts/infra/${TEST_SCRIPT}"

      - name: Configure compile cache
        if: matrix.kind != 'aot' && matrix.kind != 'cpu'
        env:
          S3_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET || 'flashinfer-build-cache' }}
          S3_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION || 'us-west-2' }}
          UPLOAD_ROLE: ${{ vars.COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN }}
        run: |
          # Shared S3 layer of the compile cache (see ci/compile_cache_s3.sh):
          # one tarball per CI image ID, GPU and lane. A10G shards test different
          # files, so each shard is its own lane; targeted runs share the lane
          # of the bare run they narrow.
          case "${TEST_SCRIPT}" in
            task_jit_run_tests_part[1-5].sh) LANE="${TEST_SCRIPT#task_jit_run_tests_}"; LANE="${LANE%.sh}" ;;
            *) LANE=all ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "${S3_BUCKET}" ] && [ -n "${S3_REGION}" ]; then
            echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_URL=https://${S3_BUCKET}.s3.${S3_REGION}.amazonaws.com/compile-cache/main" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_LANE=${CI_GPU_NAME}/${LANE}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            # Only scheduled runs on main write, and only once an admin has
            # created the upload role. A writer compiles in a directory no
            # earlier job on this runner (any of them a pull request) can have
            # touched: a new path per job, and no shared pip cache, which PR
            # containers write as root.
            if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "schedule" ] && [ "${GITHUB_REF}" = "refs/heads/main" ] \
                && [ -n "${UPLOAD_ROLE}" ]; then
              echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR=$(mktemp -u "${RUNNER_TEMP}/compile-cache-writer.XXXXXXXX")" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              echo "CI_PIP_CACHE_DIR=" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            fi
          fi

      - name: Run Test
        if: matrix.kind != 'aot'
        env:
          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET }}
          SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION }}
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1' && secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID || '' }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1' && secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY || '' }}
          # Kernel compile cache kept across this runner's jobs (see ci/bash.sh).
          # runner.workspace is the parent of the checkout, so the Cleanup step's
          # wipe of the checkout leaves it, and on the H100 hosts it sits on the
          # large NVMe work volume rather than the small root filesystem.
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.workspace }}/flashinfer-compile-cache
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_RUNNER: ${{ runner.name }}
          # PR/manual runs consume private copies. Only scheduled runs on main
          # update seeds; main has no push trigger, so a push condition here
          # would leave every seed empty.
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'read-write' || 'read-only' }}
        run: |
          case "${TEST_SCRIPT}" in
            task_jit_run_tests_part[1-5].sh|task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh|task_run_unit_tests.sh) ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Unexpected GPU test script: ${TEST_SCRIPT}"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          # ci/bash.sh options must precede the command. The credentials are
          # forwarded by name so ci/bash.sh never echoes their values.
          DOCKER_ARGS=()
          LANE_COMMAND=("./scripts/infra/${TEST_SCRIPT}")
          if [ "${GPU_TEST_SCCACHE}" = "1" ]; then
            mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(
              -e SCCACHE_BUCKET "${SCCACHE_BUCKET}"
              -e SCCACHE_REGION "${SCCACHE_REGION}"
              -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
              -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
              -e SCCACHE_STATS_DIR /workspace/sccache-stats
            )
            LANE_COMMAND=(./scripts/infra/run_with_test_sccache.sh "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}")
          fi
          TEST_RUNNER_ARGS=()
          if [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "h100" ]; then
            TEST_RUNNER_ARGS+=(--workers-per-gpu 2)
            # The CPU Unittest lane runs tests/cpu on every run, so the H100
            # lane's tests/ collection leaves it out. ci/bash.sh appends its own
            # --ignore and forwards PYTEST_ADDOPTS into GPU containers.
            export PYTEST_ADDOPTS="${PYTEST_ADDOPTS:+${PYTEST_ADDOPTS} }--ignore=tests/cpu"
          elif [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "cpu" ]; then
            # No GPU in the container. ci/bash.sh forwards the lane identity
            # only for GPU containers, so pass it here for summary.py.
            # tests/cpu peaks near 4 GiB host RSS per file on H100, so 16
            # workers fit the CPU runners the AOT lanes use (the arm64 one has
            # 64 vCPU and ~500 GiB). More would not help: the slowest file,
            # about 250 s, sets the floor.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(
              --no-gpu
              -e CI_GPU_NAME "${CI_GPU_NAME}"
              -e CI_TEST_SCRIPT "${TEST_SCRIPT}"
              -e CI_MATRIX_CUDA "${MATRIX_CUDA}"
            )
            TEST_RUNNER_ARGS+=(--workers 16)
          fi
          # Per-build compile times, summarized by the "Summarize JIT build times"
          # step. Appended: DOCKER_ARGS already carries the sccache settings.
          mkdir -p junit
          DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e FLASHINFER_JIT_BUILD_LOG /workspace/junit/jit-builds.jsonl)
          if [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "gpu" ] && [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" = "task_run_unit_tests.sh" ]; then
            # Targeted T4 runs compile with the same Ninja parallelism as the
            # bare-run T4 script (MAX_JOBS=nproc) instead of test_utils.sh's
            # 12 GB-per-nvcc budget, which was sized for H100 and resolves to
            # MAX_JOBS=1 on these 8-vCPU / 30 GiB runners. The shard scripts have
            # run these files at nproc without an OOM, and a 9-job targeted run of
            # test_batch_prefill_kernels.py peaked at 12.3 GiB process-tree RSS.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e MAX_JOBS "$(nproc)")
          fi
          TEST_TARGETS=()
          if [ -n "${TEST_PATH_ARG:-}" ]; then
            # Read into an array and expand quoted, rather than relying on word
            # splitting: this keeps the shell safe on its own terms instead of
            # inheriting the validator's charset guarantee. Globbing is off for the
            # same reason.
            set -f
            read -r -a TEST_TARGETS <<< "${TEST_PATH_ARG}"
            set +f
          fi
          if [ "${#TEST_TARGETS[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" != "task_run_unit_tests.sh" ]; then
            # A10G shard scripts take no arguments; their pytest wrapper skips files
            # outside JIT_TEST_SCOPE. Comma-joined because ci/bash.sh word-splits
            # -e values.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e JIT_TEST_SCOPE "$(IFS=,; echo "${TEST_TARGETS[*]}")")
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}"
          elif [ "${#TEST_TARGETS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            # --test-path, not bare positionals: task_run_unit_tests.sh forwards "$@"
            # to unit_test_runner.py, whose parser takes the scope as an option (or the
            # TEST_PATH env var, which ci/bash.sh does not forward into the container).
            # Bare paths fail argument-preflight with "unrecognized arguments".
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}" "${TEST_RUNNER_ARGS[@]}" --test-path "${TEST_TARGETS[@]}"
          else
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}" "${TEST_RUNNER_ARGS[@]}"
          fi

      # Runs even when tests fail or the run is cancelled: whatever was
      # compiled is still valid. Credentials are requested only now, so they
      # never reach the test step and stay short-lived.
      - name: Get compile cache upload credentials
        if: always() && env.CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION || 'us-west-2' }}
          role-session-name: compile-cache-${{ github.run_id }}
          role-duration-seconds: 900

      - name: Upload compile cache
        if: always() && env.CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR != ''
        env:
          S3_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET || 'flashinfer-build-cache' }}
        run: |
          # Keyed by the immutable image ID, as ci/compile_cache.sh restores it.
          IMAGE_ID=$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [[ ${IMAGE_ID} =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
            bash ci/compile_cache_s3.sh upload "s3://${S3_BUCKET}/compile-cache/main" \
              "${IMAGE_ID#sha256:}" "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_LANE}" "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::image ID of ${DOCKER_IMAGE} unavailable; compile cache not uploaded"
          fi
          sudo -n rm -rf "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || rm -rf "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || true

      - name: Display sccache stats
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        run: |
          STATS_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats/sccache-stats.txt"
          if [ -s "${STATS_FILE}" ]; then
            cat "${STATS_FILE}"
          else
            echo "::warning::sccache stats were not produced"
          fi

      - name: Record sccache job metadata
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        run: |
          mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
          IMAGE_DIGESTS=$(docker image inspect --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" 2>/dev/null || printf 'unavailable')
          {
            printf 'git_commit=%s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            printf 'docker_image=%s\n' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}"
            printf 'docker_image_repo_digests=%s\n' "${IMAGE_DIGESTS}"
            printf 'matrix_cuda=%s\n' "${MATRIX_CUDA}"
            printf 'matrix_arch=%s\n' "${MATRIX_ARCH}"
            printf 'matrix_kind=%s\n' "${MATRIX_KIND}"
            printf 'test_script=%s\n' "${TEST_SCRIPT}"
          } > "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats/job-metadata.txt"

      - name: Upload sccache stats
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          # GPU lanes share a CUDA/runner pair, so they add the matrix index.
          name: ${{ matrix.kind == 'aot' && format('sccache-stats-{0}-{1}', matrix.cuda, matrix.runner[2]) || format('sccache-stats-{0}-{1}-{2}', matrix.kind, matrix.cuda, strategy.job-index) }}
          path: sccache-stats/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Summarize JIT build times
        if: always() && matrix.kind != 'aot'
        run: |
          if command -v python3 >/dev/null; then
            python3 scripts/infra/summarize_jit_builds.py junit/jit-builds.jsonl || true
            python3 scripts/infra/summarize_jit_builds.py --markdown \
              junit/jit-builds.jsonl >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::python3 unavailable on runner; JIT build summary skipped"
          fi

      - name: Make JUnit XML readable
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind != 'aot' }}
        run: |
          if [ -d junit ]; then
            sudo chmod -R a+rX junit
          fi

      - name: Upload JUnit XML and telemetry
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind != 'aot' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          # Non-H100 names add the runner SM: A10G and T4 rows can run the same script.
          name: junit-${{ (matrix.kind == 'h100' || matrix.kind == 'cpu') && matrix.kind || format('{0}-{1}', matrix.script, matrix.runner[4]) }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            junit/**/*.xml
            junit/**/*.telemetry.json
            junit/**/*.meta.json
            junit/**/*.results.json
            junit/**/*.log
            junit/**/*.memory.csv
            junit/resource-telemetry/**/*
            junit/memory_summary.csv
            junit/test_timings.csv
            junit/source_summary.csv
            junit/collection-*/*.log
            junit/jit-builds.jsonl
            junit/run-summary.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Make shard JUnit XML readable
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind == 'gpu' }}
        run: |
          if [ -d junit-shard ]; then
            sudo chmod -R a+rX junit-shard
          fi

      - name: Upload shard JUnit XML
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind == 'gpu' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            junit-shard/**/*.xml
            junit-shard/**/resource-telemetry/**/*
            junit-shard/**/*.memory.csv
            junit-shard/**/memory_summary.csv
            junit-shard/**/test_timings.csv
            junit-shard/**/source_summary.csv
            junit-shard/**/run-summary.json
            junit-shard/**/*.telemetry.json
            junit-shard/**/*.meta.json
            junit-shard/**/*.results.json
            junit-shard/**/*.log
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Provider spec lint - quick CUDA-target check ahead of the AOT builds
  #
  # The AOT lanes build every provider wheel (hours). The release builds reject a
  # provider whose modules carry another architecture's CUDA target or PTX, which
  # a PR used to find out only from the nightly. This generates each provider's
  # spec list (no compiling, no GPU) and checks the explicit -gencode flags. The
  # AOT lanes repeat it first thing, so their fail-fast still stops the matrix.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  spec-lint:
    name: Provider Spec Lint (${{ matrix.cuda }})
    needs: [gate, setup]
    if: |
      needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.skip_build != 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.spec_lint_count != '0'
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, cpu, on-demand]
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.spec_lint_matrix) }}
    env:
      DOCKER_IMAGE: flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${{ matrix.cuda }}:${{ needs.setup.outputs.docker_tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Cleanup
        run: |
          docker ps -q | xargs -r docker stop 2>/dev/null || true
          docker ps -aq | xargs -r docker rm 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo rm -rf "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:?}"/* || true
          sudo rm -rf "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:?}"/.[!.]* || true
          docker image prune -f || true

      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.checkout_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Prepare selected source and submodules
        env:
          SELECTED_BASE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_base }}
          SELECTED_TREE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SELECTED_BASE" ]; then
            [[ "$SELECTED_BASE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "$SELECTED_TREE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
            PINNED_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = true ]; then
              git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin "$PINNED_HEAD" "$SELECTED_BASE"
            fi
            git cat-file -e "${SELECTED_BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$SELECTED_BASE"
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$PINNED_HEAD"
            [ "$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')" = "$SELECTED_TREE" ]
          fi
          git submodule update --init --recursive

      - name: Lint provider spec CUDA targets
        run: bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" --no-gpu ./scripts/infra/task_check_jit_spec_gencodes.sh

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Test Results Summary
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  test-results-summary:
    name: Test Results Summary
    if: "!cancelled()"
    needs:
      - gate
      - setup
      - test
      - spec-lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check Authorization
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized != 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check skip patterns for unauthorized PRs
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized != 'true'
        id: skip-check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"

          SKIP=true
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then
              SKIP=false
              break
            fi
          done <<< "$CHANGED"

          echo "skip=$SKIP" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Report unauthorized PR status
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          echo "## Test Results Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

          if [ "${{ steps.skip-check.outputs.skip }}" == "true" ]; then
            echo "CI not required (docs/config only changes)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "::notice::Docs-only PR — no CI needed"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Don't turn an already-passing commit red for an event that changed no
          # code - re-earning that green costs another full GPU run. A code change
          # produces a new SHA with no prior run, so this cannot report untested
          # code as passing.
          PASSED=$(gh run list \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --workflow "${{ github.workflow }}" \
            --commit "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --status success \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null) || PASSED=0

          if [ "${PASSED:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "CI already passed for this commit ($HEAD_SHA)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "::notice::Keeping the passing result already recorded for this commit"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Failing while another run tests this commit would turn the required
          # check red under it, so report what that run reports. Older runs only,
          # so two label events cannot wait on each other.
          ACTIVE=$(gh run list \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --workflow "${{ github.workflow }}" \
            --commit "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --limit 50 \
            --json databaseId,status \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.databaseId < (env.GITHUB_RUN_ID | tonumber))
                       | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued")]
                  | min_by(.databaseId) | .databaseId // empty' 2>/dev/null) || ACTIVE=""

          if [ -n "$ACTIVE" ]; then
            RUN_URL="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/$ACTIVE"
            echo "Tests for this commit are running in [run $ACTIVE]($RUN_URL)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

            # The summary lands only when this job ends, so the annotation is
            # what carries the link on the PR meanwhile.
            echo "::notice title=Tests are already running for this commit::$RUN_URL"

            # No wait limit, because any number here would guess at test duration
            # and guessing low fails a healthy run. The wait ends when the
            # followed run concludes, or when it stops being readable.
            CONCLUSION=""
            UNREADABLE=0
            while true; do
              INFO=$(gh run view "$ACTIVE" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
                --json status,conclusion,jobs \
                --jq '.status + "|" + (.conclusion // "") + "|"
                      + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "completed")] | length | tostring) + " done, "
                      + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring) + " running, "
                      + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "queued")] | length | tostring) + " waiting for a runner, of "
                      + (.jobs | length | tostring) + " jobs"' 2>/dev/null) || INFO=""
              IFS='|' read -r STATUS CONCLUSION PROGRESS <<< "$INFO"

              if [ "$STATUS" == "completed" ]; then
                break
              fi

              # Transient errors retry; 5 minutes unreadable means the run is
              # gone and no conclusion is coming.
              if [ -z "$STATUS" ]; then
                UNREADABLE=$((UNREADABLE + 1))
                if [ "$UNREADABLE" -ge 10 ]; then
                  echo "Result: run $ACTIVE is no longer readable" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
                  exit 1
                fi
              else
                UNREADABLE=0
              fi

              echo "run $ACTIVE after $((SECONDS / 60))m: ${PROGRESS:-progress unavailable} - $RUN_URL"
              sleep 30
            done

            if [ "$CONCLUSION" == "success" ] || [ "$CONCLUSION" == "skipped" ]; then
              echo "Result: Tests Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Result: run $ACTIVE ended as '${CONCLUSION:-still running}'" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "CI skipped (pending authorization)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "A contributor who can label the PR, or a \`ci-users\` member, can comment \`@flashinfer-bot run\` to start CI." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "This is also needed after pushing new commits, since CI no longer starts on its own." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "::warning::CI skipped — pending authorization"
          exit 1

      - name: Checkout (for skip-all analysis)
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download H100 JUnit artifacts
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && needs.test.result != 'cancelled'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: junit-h100-*
          path: junit-h100
          merge-multiple: true
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Download CPU JUnit artifacts
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && needs.test.result != 'cancelled'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: junit-cpu-*
          path: junit-cpu
          merge-multiple: true
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Download shard JUnit artifacts (A10G/T4)
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && needs.test.result != 'cancelled'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: junit-shard-*
          path: junit-shards
          merge-multiple: true
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Check skip-all test files
        id: skip-all
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          SUMMARY_ARGS=""
          if [ -f junit-h100/run-summary.json ]; then
            SUMMARY_ARGS="--summary junit-h100/run-summary.json"
          fi
          # The CPU lane runs the same sharded runner, so it has a run summary.
          if [ -f junit-cpu/run-summary.json ]; then
            SUMMARY_ARGS="$SUMMARY_ARGS --summary junit-cpu/run-summary.json --junit-dir junit-cpu"
          fi

          # A10G/T4 shard lanes produce raw JUnit XML (no run-summary.json).
          # Discover them from the merged download directory.
          SHARD_ARGS=""
          if [ -d junit-shards ]; then
            # The merged artifact flattens all shard uploads into one tree.
            # Infer lane names from the XML paths: the shard scripts write
            # junit-shard/tests/..., so after merge we get
            # junit-shards/tests/... from each lane.  Since the download
            # merges all lanes into one directory, we label the combined
            # tree as "A10G+T4" — individual lane attribution would require
            # per-lane artifact naming, which the shard scripts don't do.
            SHARD_ARGS="--junit-xml-lane A10G+T4 junit-shards"
          fi

          if [ -z "$SUMMARY_ARGS" ] && [ -z "$SHARD_ARGS" ]; then
            echo "No JUnit artifacts found; skipping skip-all check"
            echo "skip_all_found=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          SKIP_ALL_EXIT=0
          REPORT=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/check_skip_all.py \
            --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
            $SUMMARY_ARGS \
            $SHARD_ARGS \
            --junit-dir junit-h100 \
            --github-actions 2>&1) || SKIP_ALL_EXIT=$?
          echo "$REPORT"

          if [ "$SKIP_ALL_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::check_skip_all.py failed with exit code $SKIP_ALL_EXIT"
            exit "$SKIP_ALL_EXIT"
          fi
          echo "$REPORT"

          if echo "$REPORT" | grep -qF "⚠️ **skip-all**"; then
            echo "skip_all_found=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "skip_all_found=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

          # Append to step summary.
          {
            echo ""
            echo "$REPORT"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          # Save the report for the PR comment step.
          echo "$REPORT" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/skip-all-report.md"

      - name: Comment on PR about skip-all findings
        if: steps.skip-all.outputs.skip_all_found == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          # Build comment body from the saved report.
          {
            echo "⚠️ **Skip-all detection (IKL-569)**"
            echo ""
            echo "Some changed test files had **all nodes skipped** on every CI lane."
            echo "This means CI passed without executing any of the new or modified tests."
            echo ""
            echo "<details>"
            echo "<summary>Full report</summary>"
            echo ""
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/skip-all-report.md"
            echo ""
            echo "</details>"
            echo ""
            echo "Please check whether the skipped tests are expected (e.g. SM arch not"
            echo "available on any lane) or indicate a gap in CI coverage."
          } > "$RUNNER_TEMP/skip-all-comment.md"

          # Avoid duplicate comments on re-runs by deleting any prior bot comment
          # with our marker.
          EXISTING=$(gh api \
            "/repos/${{ github.repository }}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" \
            --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.user.login == "github-actions[bot]") | select(.body | contains("Skip-all detection (IKL-569)")) | .id')
          for ID in $EXISTING; do
            gh api -X DELETE "/repos/${{ github.repository }}/issues/comments/${ID}" || true
          done

          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/skip-all-comment.md"

      - name: Check trace reference coverage
        id: trace-coverage
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          TRACE_EXIT=0
          REPORT=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/check_trace_coverage.py \
            --github-actions 2>&1) || TRACE_EXIT=$?
          echo "$REPORT"

          if [ "$TRACE_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::check_trace_coverage.py failed with exit code $TRACE_EXIT"
            exit "$TRACE_EXIT"
          fi
          echo "$REPORT"
          {
            echo ""
            echo "$REPORT"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          if echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "gap"; then
            echo "trace_gaps=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "trace_gaps=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Check Results
        if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
        env:
          # Bound, not interpolated into the script body. The value originates from a
          # commit status description, which anything holding statuses:write can set;
          # TARGET_RE happens to exclude quotes and backticks, but that guarantee lives
          # in another file and must not be what keeps this step from being injectable.
          TEST_SCOPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.test_scope }}
          SKIP_ALL_FOUND: ${{ steps.skip-all.outputs.skip_all_found }}
          TRACE_GAPS: ${{ steps.trace-coverage.outputs.trace_gaps }}
          H100_DISABLED: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.h100_disabled }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          TEST_MATRIX: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.test_matrix }}
        run: |
          echo "## Test Results Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

          # A failed setup leaves the tests skipped and skip_build empty, which
          # would otherwise reach the "skipped counts as passed" branch below
          # and report success for a run where nothing was tested.
          SETUP="${{ needs.setup.result }}"
          if [ "$SETUP" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Setup did not succeed (result: $SETUP), so no tests ran" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "Result: Tests Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "${{ needs.setup.outputs.skip_build }}" == "true" ]; then
            echo "Build skipped (docs/config only changes)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            exit 0
          fi

          # Every test is one entry of a single matrix, so this is the aggregate
          # result. Per-test outcomes are on the individual checks.
          RESULT="${{ needs.test.result }}"
          echo "Tests: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.test_count }}, result: $RESULT" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

          # A matrix failure hides cancelled siblings in needs.test.result. Read
          # this attempt only; diagnostics must not change the required verdict.
          if [ "${{ needs.setup.outputs.test_count }}" != "0" ]; then
            if timeout 20s gh api --paginate \
                "/repos/$GH_REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/attempts/$RUN_ATTEMPT/jobs?per_page=100" \
                --jq '{jobs: [.jobs[] | {name, run_id, run_attempt, status, conclusion, html_url}]}' \
                > "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-lane-jobs.json" && \
              jq -nr --argjson matrix "$TEST_MATRIX" \
                --argjson run "$RUN_ID" --argjson attempt "$RUN_ATTEMPT" \
                --slurpfile pages "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-lane-jobs.json" '
                  [$pages[].jobs[] | select(.run_id == $run and .run_attempt == $attempt)] as $jobs
                  | [$matrix.include[].name as $name
                     | [$jobs[] | select(.name == $name)] as $matches
                     | if ($matches | length) != 1 then
                         {name: $name, result: (if ($matches | length) == 0 then "missing" else "unknown" end)}
                       else $matches[0]
                         | .result = (if .status != "completed" then (.status // "unknown") else (.conclusion // "unknown") end)
                       end] as $lanes
                  | "### Matrix lane outcomes (attempt \($attempt))", "",
                    ($lanes | group_by(.result) | map("\(length) \(.[0].result)") | join(", ")), "",
                    (if any($lanes[]; .result != "success") then
                       "Coverage is incomplete. Cancelled, skipped, missing or unfinished lanes do not establish passing coverage."
                     else "All planned matrix lanes completed successfully." end), "",
                    "| Lane | Outcome | Details |", "| --- | --- | --- |",
                    ($lanes | sort_by(if .result == "failure" then 0 elif .result == "success" then 2 else 1 end)[]
                     | "| \(.name) | \(.result) | \(if .html_url then "[Open job](\(.html_url))" else "Unavailable" end) |"), ""
                ' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-lane-summary.md"; then
              cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-lane-summary.md" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            else
              echo "Matrix lane outcomes unavailable (API or metadata error); per-lane coverage is unknown." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            fi
          fi

          # A scope is sticky per SHA: re-applying run-ci by hand on a commit that
          # once had a scoped bot run silently reuses it, so this required check can
          # go green having run three narrow lanes. The job names change from "JIT
          # Unittest" to "Targeted Unittest", but that is easy to miss on a check
          # list -- say it outright on the check a merge decision actually reads.
          # The H100 lane is temporarily off on PRs (see Build Test Matrix). A scope
          # only H100 covered now schedules nothing and passes, so say so here.
          if [ "$H100_DISABLED" == "true" ]; then
            echo "> **H100 lane temporarily disabled on PRs** — H100 tests run only in scheduled main runs and manual workflow_dispatch runs." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi

          if [ -n "${TEST_SCOPE:-}" ]; then
            echo "> **Scoped run — NOT the full suite.**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> Tested only: \`${TEST_SCOPE}\`, plus \`tests/cpu\` on the CPU lane" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> Comment \`@flashinfer-bot run all\` for full coverage." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi

          if [ "$SKIP_ALL_FOUND" == "true" ]; then
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> ⚠️ **Some changed test files had all nodes skipped on every lane.**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> See the skip-all report above for details." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi

          if [ "$TRACE_GAPS" == "true" ]; then
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> ⚠️ **Some GDN/KDA trace definitions are missing numerical coverage.**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "> See the trace coverage report above for details." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi

          # The provider spec lint is its own job, so the matrix result above does
          # not cover it; a skipped lint (no published image, skip_aot) is not a failure.
          SPEC_LINT="${{ needs.spec-lint.result }}"
          echo "Provider spec lint: $SPEC_LINT" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if [ "$SPEC_LINT" == "failure" ] || [ "$SPEC_LINT" == "cancelled" ]; then
            echo "Result: Tests Failed" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "$RESULT" == "success" ] || [ "$RESULT" == "skipped" ]; then
            echo "Result: Tests Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            exit 0
          fi

          # fail-fast stops the siblings as soon as one entry fails, so any
          # cancelled test means "stopped early", not "flaky".
          echo "Result: Tests Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          exit 1

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Report scheduled main results - one open tracking issue while main is red
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  report-main-status:
    name: Report Main Status
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' && !cancelled()
    needs: [test-results-summary]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      RESULT: ${{ needs.test-results-summary.result }}
      RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
      RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
      SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      TITLE: "Scheduled PR Test is failing on main"
    steps:
      - name: Open, update or close the tracking issue
        run: |
          # A re-run keeps its run ID, so an old run re-run late must not override
          # the result of a newer scheduled run that has already finished.
          NEWER=$(gh run list --workflow pr-test.yml --event schedule --branch main \
            --status completed --limit 20 --json databaseId \
            --jq "map(select(.databaseId > $RUN_ID)) | length")
          if [ "$NEWER" != "0" ]; then
            echo "A newer scheduled run has already finished; leaving the issue to it"
            exit 0
          fi

          ISSUE=$(gh issue list --state open --search "in:title \"$TITLE\"" \
            --json number,title --jq "map(select(.title == \"$TITLE\"))[0].number // empty")

          if [ "$RESULT" == "success" ]; then
            if [ -n "$ISSUE" ]; then
              gh issue close "$ISSUE" --comment "Green again at $SHA: $RUN_URL"
            fi
            exit 0
          fi

          BODY="Scheduled run on \`$SHA\` failed: $RUN_URL"
          if [ -n "$ISSUE" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$ISSUE" --body "$BODY"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$TITLE" \
              --body "$BODY. This issue gets a comment per failed run and closes on the next green one."
          fi
trusted_ci.scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_sc:
"""Narrow a targeted CI scope to what a lane's bare run covers.

A targeted run on a lane never tests more than that lane's bare run. The A10G and
T4 bare runs use ``scripts/task_jit_run_tests_part*.sh`` and
``scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh``, respectively,
so their targeted scope is the requested paths intersected with the ``pytest``
targets of those scripts. Reading the scripts keeps them the single source of
truth: adding a file to a shard covers it on every bare run and makes it eligible
for targeted runs on that lane. (H100's bare run covers ``tests/``, so it needs no
narrowing and does not use this tool.)

Only ``pytest ... tests/...`` lines count. Wrapper commands such as
``bash tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh unit`` run a curated subset with their own
flags, so they do not make their directory eligible.

Usage::

    targeted_lane_scope.py --scripts scripts/task_jit_run_tests_part{1..5}.sh \\
        --targets "tests/attention/ tests/utils/test_topk.py"

Prints the narrowed scope on one line; an empty line means nothing requested is
covered and the lane should not be scheduled. Targets are files or directories
under ``tests/`` (``::`` selectors are rejected upstream by
``experimental_test_scope.py``). A shard script with no parseable ``pytest`` line
is a parser-drift bug, not an empty scope, and exits non-zero; ``pr-test.yml``
runs ``--coverage-only`` on every setup so such drift fails the PR that causes it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

_PYTEST_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*pytest\b(?:\s+-\S+)*\s+(tests/\S+)")


def _norm(path: str) -> str:
    """``./tests/x/`` -> ``tests/x``."""
    path = path.strip()
    return PurePosixPath(path).as_posix() if path else ""


def _is_test_file(path: str) -> bool:
    # Targets are not existence-checked, so classify by shape.
    return PurePosixPath(path).suffix == ".py"


def _within(path: str, directory: str) -> bool:
    # Component-wise: tests/att does not contain tests/attention/x.py.
    return PurePosixPath(path).is_relative_to(PurePosixPath(directory))


def coverage(scripts: list[Path]) -> list[str]:
    """Test files the shard scripts run, in script order, without duplicates."""
    files: dict[str, None] = {}  # insertion-ordered set
    unparsed: list[str] = []
    for script in scripts:
        matches = filter(None, map(_PYTEST_LINE.match, script.read_text().splitlines()))
        targets = [_norm(m.group(1)) for m in matches]
        if not targets:
            unparsed.append(str(script))
        files.update(dict.fromkeys(targets))
    # Checked per script: with five A10G shards, one drifting to an unparsed
    # invocation would leave the total non-empty and silently drop its files.
    if unparsed:
        raise ValueError(
            f"no pytest targets parsed from {', '.join(unparsed)} -- parser drift?"
        )
    return list(files)


def intersect(targets: list[str], covered: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Requested files kept if covered; requested directories become their covered files."""
    selected: dict[str, None] = {}  # insertion-ordered set
    for target in filter(None, map(_norm, targets)):
        if _is_test_file(target):
            if target in covered:
                selected[target] = None
        else:
            selected.update(dict.fromkeys(f for f in covered if _within(f, target)))
    return list(selected)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n", 1)[0])
    ap.add_argument(
        "--scripts",
        nargs="+",
        type=Path,
        help="shard scripts defining the lane's coverage",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--targets",
        default="",
        help="requested scope: space-separated paths under tests/",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--coverage-only",
        action="store_true",
        help="print the coverage instead of the intersection",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.selftest:
        return _selftest()
    if not args.scripts:
        ap.error("--scripts is required (or use --selftest)")
    missing = [str(s) for s in args.scripts if not s.is_file()]
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"targeted_lane_scope: shard script not found: {', '.join(missing)}")
    try:
        covered = coverage(args.scripts)
    except ValueError as exc:
        sys.exit(f"targeted_lane_scope: {exc}")
    print(
        " ".join(
            covered if args.coverage_only else intersect(args.targets.split(), covered)
        )
    )
    return 0


def _selftest() -> int:
    import tempfile

    failures: list[str] = []

    def check(name: str, got: object, want: object) -> None:
        if got != want:
            failures.append(f"{name}: got {got!r}, want {want!r}")

    def raises(name: str, exc_type: type[BaseException], fn) -> BaseException | None:
        try:
            fn()
        except exc_type as exc:
            return exc
        failures.append(f"{name}: expected {exc_type.__name__}")
        return None

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        part = Path(td) / "part.sh"
        part.write_text(
            "#!/bin/bash\n"
            "set -x\n"
            "# pytest -s tests/commented_out.py\n"
            "bash tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh unit\n"
            "pytest -s tests/attention/test_a.py\n"
            "  pytest -s -x tests/utils/test_b.py\n"
            "pytest tests/gemm/test_c.py\n"
        )
        cov = coverage([part])
        a, b, c = (
            "tests/attention/test_a.py",
            "tests/utils/test_b.py",
            "tests/gemm/test_c.py",
        )
        check(
            "coverage: pytest lines only, comments and wrappers ignored", cov, [a, b, c]
        )
        check("file in coverage", intersect([b], cov), [b])
        check("file not in coverage", intersect(["tests/kda/test_x.py"], cov), [])
        check(
            "directory expands to covered files",
            intersect(["tests/attention/"], cov),
            [a],
        )
        check(
            "directory without trailing slash", intersect(["tests/attention"], cov), [a]
        )
        check("tests/ expands to everything", intersect(["tests/"], cov), cov)
        check(
            "wrapper-run directory is not covered",
            intersect(["tests/moe_ep/"], cov),
            [],
        )
        check(
            "order kept, uncovered dropped, deduplicated",
            intersect(["tests/gemm/", "tests/kda/", c], cov),
            [c],
        )
        check("./ prefix normalised", intersect(["./" + b], cov), [b])
        check("path prefix is not containment", intersect(["tests/att"], cov), [])

        drifted = Path(td) / "drifted.sh"
        drifted.write_text("#!/bin/bash\npython -m pytest tests/attention/test_a.py\n")
        exc = raises("unparsed shard rejected", ValueError, lambda: coverage([drifted]))
        exc = raises(
            "one unparsed shard among parsed ones rejected",
            ValueError,
            lambda: coverage([part, drifted]),
        )
        if exc:
            check("error names the unparsed script", str(drifted) in str(exc), True)
            check("error does not name the parsed script", str(part) in str(exc), False)
        exc = raises(
            "main: unparsed shard exits non-zero",
            SystemExit,
            lambda: main(["--scripts", str(drifted)]),
        )
        if exc:
            check("main: unparsed shard exit code is an error", bool(exc.code), True)
        check(
            "main: empty intersection exits zero",
            main(["--scripts", str(part), "--targets", "tests/kda/x.py"]),
            0,
        )

    for failure in failures:
        print(failure)
    print("selftest: FAILED" if failures else "selftest: all cases pass")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
